description: WS2812/SK6812 stream monitor over measured bit-times, one bit-time per accepted beat. a[15:0]=the high ticks of the bit-time and a[31:16]=the low ticks, both in 125 ns units, so a nominal 1.25 us bit is 10 ticks. b[7:0]=PIXELS, the pixel count a latched frame must have (0 disables the length check), b[31:8] must be zero. c[1:0]=TOL, the extra ticks allowed on either side of the 9..11 tick period window, c[11:6]=RSTU, the latch threshold in units of 16 ticks (0 means the published 400 ticks, i.e. 50 us), c[29:12] must be zero, c[30]=1 closes the frame on this beat (a manual latch) and c[31]=1 clears the shift register, the bit position, the pixel count, the frame digest and every counter before this beat is processed. A beat whose total is at least the latch threshold, or which requests a manual latch, takes no bit: it latches the pixel stream if anything is present, so a partial pixel in the shift register is a truncated-frame violation and a count that differs from PIXELS is a frame-length violation, and both then reset the accumulation. Otherwise the bit is decoded by the published duty threshold (high ticks at or above 5 of 10 is a 1) and shifted in MSB-first; a duty window is legal for a 0 at high 1..4 with low 5..8 and for a 1 at high 5..8 with low 2..5, so any other combination is a duty violation that is still decoded, and a total outside 9-TOL to 11+TOL is a period violation that is still decoded. The 24th bit completes a pixel: it is stored as the last pixel, increments the pixel count and XORs its three channels into the frame digest. result[7:0]=blue of the last completed pixel, result[15:8]=red, result[23:16]=green, result[24]=a bit was accepted, result[25]=the decoded bit value, result[26]=a pixel was completed, result[27]=the frame latched, result[28]=duty violation, result[29]=period violation, result[30]=frame-length violation, result[31]=truncated pixel. aux[7:0]=the frame digest, aux[15:8]=the pixel count, aux[23:16]=the bit position, aux[24]=restart applied, aux[25]=manual latch requested, aux[26]=a frame is valid, aux[27]=latch with nothing pending, aux[31:28]=duty violation count [3:0]. State: shift register state[23:0], bit position state[29:24], pixel count state[37:30], frame digest state[45:38], last pixel state[69:46], frame valid state[70], saturating latch count state[78:71], saturating duty violation count state[86:79], saturating period violation count state[94:87], saturating frame-length violation count state[102:95], saturating truncation violation count state[110:103], saturating beat count state[118:111]. Any duty, period, length or truncation violation faults.
hardware_advantage: Ten duty window compares, a 24-bit MSB-first shift and the latch threshold resolve on the enabled edge that carries the bit-time, so a stripped controller can watch a whole WS2812 chain for dropped bits at full data rate, which a bit-banged CPU loop cannot do at all because its own microsecond-scale jitter is the thing it would have to measure.
